elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims concerning the services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Paragraph 7(d) requires Contractor to indemnify Company against any third-party claim that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate an intellectual-property right.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims to the extent caused by Customer's modifications.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims to the extent caused by combinations with items not supplied by Vendor.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims to the extent caused by Customer's specifications.

elements.element: For a covered IP claim, Vendor must procure Customer's right to continue using the affected item.

elements.element: For a covered IP claim, Vendor must have the option or obligation to modify the affected item so it is non-infringing.

elements.element: For a covered IP claim, Vendor must have the option or obligation to replace the affected item with a non-infringing item.
elements.evidence: Paragraph 7(d) requires Contractor to replace the affected item so that it is non-infringing as one available remedy.

elements.element: If procurement, modification, and replacement are unavailable, Vendor must refund the fees paid for the affected item.
elements.evidence: Paragraph 7(d) requires a refund of fees paid for the affected item if the other remedies are not commercially available.

elements.element: Vendor's aggregate liability for the IP indemnity must be subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees rather than the ordinary liability cap.
elements.evidence: Paragraph 7(d) applies notwithstanding Paragraph 7(a) and caps aggregate liability under 7(d) at three times the annual fees paid under the Agreement.

result.reason: The added paragraph fully implements the fallback IP indemnity, all three stated exclusions, the procure/modify/replace/refund remedy sequence, and an express 3× annual-fees super-cap overriding Paragraph 7(a). It does not satisfy the preferred position because it omits defense duties, affiliate protection, breach-of-law, Vendor-caused data-breach and gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct coverage, and all indemnity procedures. The change is not minimal because the existing warranty subsection is unnecessarily relocated before the Section 7 heading. Although the added paragraph itself is generally clear and preserves the other liability terms through an express override, the rendered structure is seriously defective: subsection (c) appears before its section heading, the pre-existing duplicate subsection numbering remains, and the heading still refers to indemnification of Contractor even though the operative indemnity is by Contractor.
